column1: # Opcode -> payload field widths, v3 (round 474). Generated by tools/payload_sweep.py.
# Each row: opcode, the function that sends it, field count, widths in address
# order. VAR means the tool declined -- an intervening call may have clobbered
#   A  mov reg,[this+0x278] ; push <opcode> ; call reg      (opens, then appends)
#   B  mov reg,[buf+0x1050] ; mov WORD PTR [reg],<opcode>   (opens, then appends)
#   C  mov ecx,<opcode> ; call Msg_SendTwoFieldReply        (the HELPER opens)
# C was missing until round 474: such a caller sends without ever opening a
# message, so a sweep keyed on opens misses it by construction. Its payload is
# the grounded {u8, u16} of round 443, and a C row is emitted only where no
# direct-open row exists for the same (opcode, function).
#  * Attribution is by ADDRESS ORDER, a heuristic: an append on a branch can
#    textually follow an open it does not belong to.
#  * 1,086 appends across 274 functions have no open before them in their own
#    function -- opened inside some other helper -- and are omitted, not guessed.
#  * Widths only. Nothing here says what a field MEANS.
# comparable opcodes: 99% agree with the client on field 1, 89% prefix-match,
